sections.h2: Hours and cutoffs at the Alpena County recording desk
sections.html:
The register works out of 720 W. Chisholm Street, Suite 4, and answers at 989-354-9547 (fax 989-354-9646). Hours run 8 a.m. until 4:30 p.m. on weekdays.

Recording cutoffs come sooner than closing time. An e-filing must land by 3:30 p.m. to count that day, and paper has until 4:00 p.m. at the window. Anything later joins the next business day's pile, so a Friday 4:15 delivery waits for Monday.

The register insists on originals. Once indexed, the original is returned to the sender, normally inside seven days of recording. No blank deeds are given out, and staff cannot coach you through completing one. Visit an office supply store, a lawyer or a title company for that.

A deed that is ready early saves trouble. Sellers who sign on a Friday afternoon often find the paper waits until Monday, so plan the signing and the delivery for earlier in the day and earlier in the week.

Most Michigan counties follow MCL 600.2567, which prices a recording at one flat sum no matter the number of pages. A charter county can override that by ordinance, so phone the register for the exact total before a check goes in the mail.

  • $30 for every recorded paper, and $3 more for each extra instrument it assigns or discharges.
  • Copies at $1 per page and certification at $5.
  • Index searches at 50 cents a year for grantor and grantee names, never less than $5.
  • A tax certification fee on certain deeds. Ask the Alpena County treasurer whether yours qualifies.

The county office page links to a fee sheet, a recording requirements sheet and e-recording instructions.

Researchers can choose Laredo or Tapestry. Tapestry fits someone who needs a copy or two, and Laredo suits title companies and frequent searchers.

Two free services cover Alpena County only: a property fraud alert and a notary fraud alert. Each sends a call, text or email when a recorded paper carries your name.

The same office is a certified passport agent and takes passport photos, so some visitors are there for a passport. If you want to watch for fraud, sign up for the property alert at no cost, and add the notary alert if you often use a notary.

sections.h2: What will state and county transfer tax cost on an Alpena County house?
sections.html:
On each $500 of value, the seller pays 55 cents to the county (MCL 207.504) and $3.75 to the state (MCL 207.525). A partial $500 counts as a full one.

Transfer tax rates on an Alpena County sale
LevelRate per $500Paid to
County$0.55County treasurer
State$3.75County treasurer, for the state
Both$4.30County treasurer

Remit it to the Alpena County treasurer inside 15 days after delivery. When furniture or equipment rides along, only the real estate is taxed, as long as the deed or an attached affidavit lists the values separately. The county treasurer is also the person to ask about any tax still owed on the parcel, so call before you pick a closing date.

sections.h2: Distress and court transfers that escape the tax
sections.html:
Distressed owners and heirs should read MCL 207.526, because several exemptions fit their situations.

  • A deed handed to a lender in foreclosure or in place of it. The lender's own resale is still taxed.
  • A court of record's order moving title, when no price is set.
  • An installment land contract, while legal title sits with the seller.
  • Husband and wife moving property into or out of a tenancy by the entireties.

Paid in error? Treasury takes refund requests.

sections.h2: What details on a deed trip up a recording?
sections.html:
Michigan's recording act, MCL 565.201, lets a register refuse a paper that skips basic identification steps. Returns usually trace to one of these:

  • A signer's printed name that differs from the name in the notary's certificate.
  • Ink that is not black or dark blue.
  • No notary name printed next to the notary's signature.
  • No street address for the buyer, or no drafter name and address.
  • A full Social Security number left visible.
  • Foreign-language text without an English version attached.

Once a paper satisfies the act, the register has no right to refuse it over what it says.

sections.h2: Timing a deed against the cutoffs
sections.html:
Start the e-record by early afternoon, because the 3:30 p.m. cutoff arrives half an hour before the counter's 4:00. Before signing, run through a short list:

  • The buyer's mailing address appears on the deed.
  • The notary's name is printed beside the signature.
  • The full sale value is stated, or a value affidavit is attached.
  • The original, not a copy, goes to the register.
  • Any tax certification step has been cleared with the county treasurer.

Miss the cutoff and your record date moves to the next business day. On a closing that depends on recording, that can mean a weekend wait, so plan the signing for the morning.

sections.h2: Alpena County for a home seller
sections.html:
Alpena County sits in the northeast of Michigan's Lower Peninsula, fronting Lake Huron and Thunder Bay. Alpena is the county seat and its only city, and Hillman is a village that straddles the county line. U.S. 23 hugs the shoreline, M-32 ends in downtown Alpena, and M-65 offers a quicker way south. About 28,853 people live here, and four of every five homes are lived in by their owners.

Assessments are a local matter, so a seller with a parcel question should call the city or township assessor, not the register. Many properties are lakefront or inherited, so expect a buyer to ask about survey, access and tax history. The county recorded 72 building permits in 2025, and permit questions go to the local building office.

sections.h2: Selling an Alpena County house: a short plan
sections.html:
1. Ask the county treasurer about the tax balance and whether a tax certification applies to your deed.
  2. Have a lawyer or title company prepare the deed, since the register cannot.
  3. Check the deed against the list above: names, ink, notary, buyer address and sale value.
  4. Pick e-recording or paper, and send it before the cutoff.
  5. Watch for the returned original within about seven days of recording.

If the house is inherited, behind on tax or in poor shape, a cash as-is sale can shorten the wait for a buyer's loan. Treat any offer as one option and compare it with what a listing would net after repairs, commission and months of carrying costs. Whichever route you take, keep a copy of the recorded deed.

faqs.q: What is the last time of day to record a deed in Alpena County?
faqs.a: Paper filings are taken until 4:00 p.m. and e-recordings until 3:30 p.m. A deed that arrives later is recorded on the next business day.

faqs.q: How can I contact the Alpena County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: Phone 989-354-9547 or fax 989-354-9646, or visit 720 W. Chisholm Street, Suite 4, in Alpena.

faqs.q: Will my original deed come back from the Alpena County register?
faqs.a: Yes. The office indexes the paper and then returns the original, usually within a week of the recording date.

faqs.q: How much transfer tax applies to an Alpena County sale?
faqs.a: The seller pays $0.55 per $500 to the county and $3.75 per $500 to the state, which is $4.30 together. Each rate applies to every $500 or fraction thereof.

faqs.q: Can Alpena County staff write or advise on my deed?
faqs.a: No. They do not complete documents, give legal advice or provide blank deeds. A title company, an attorney or an office supply store can help instead.
